issues.legal_issue: Eviction for an unsafe or unfit building is justified only when the necessary repairs or building work require the tenant to vacate.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises had become unsafe and unfit for human habitation.
The evidence showed that part of the roof had fallen, while the remaining repairs were limited.
The lower appellate authority found that the work was not extensive and that the tenant could remain in possession while repairs were carried out.
issues.conclusion: The need for eviction depends on whether the repairs or structural work are so fundamental and extensive that they cannot be carried out while the tenant remains in possession; work that can be completed without displacing the tenant does not justify eviction on this ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(3)(a)(iii) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, must be read with section 13(4), which requires restoration of possession to the evicted tenant after the relevant work. In Maharaj Jagat Bahadur Singh v. Badri Prasad Seth, the Court held that eviction is attracted only when the building must be vacated to carry out the work. Piara Lal v. Kewal Krishan Chopra likewise considered whether damage to part of a building showed that it as a whole was unsafe and unfit.

predicates.unsafe_building_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction because a building is alleged to be unsafe or unfit for human habitation.
predicates.repair_work_requires_vacancy: The necessary work cannot be carried out while the tenant remains in possession.
predicates.repair_work_is_fundamental_and_extensive: The necessary work is fundamental and extensive rather than limited or ordinary.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction because a building is unsafe or unfit, eviction for repairs may be ordered if the work is fundamental and extensive and requires the tenant to vacate.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent repair that makes the premises safe and fit for habitation can extinguish the need for eviction, even when the tenant completed the repair without first obtaining permission through the statutory repair procedure.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction because the premises had become unsafe and unfit after part of the roof fell.
The tenant replaced the fallen portion of the roof, and the repair was found to make the premises safe and fit for habitation.
The repair was minor and did not amount to reconstruction or structural alteration.
The High Court accepted the finding that the tenant had repaired the roof but restored the eviction order because the tenant had not followed the statutory procedure for repairs.
issues.conclusion: Once the tenant's repairs made the premises safe and fit for habitation, the need for eviction on that ground no longer subsisted; the appellate authority could take that subsequent event into account, and the eviction order was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13(3)(a)(iii) and 13(4) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, must be read harmoniously, so that the landlord's right to seek possession for necessary work is consistent with the evicted tenant's right to restoration after the work. Section 12 provides the statutory procedure for a tenant to seek permission to make necessary repairs when the landlord fails to do so; section 108(f) of the Transfer of Property Act addresses a tenant's repair rights and recovery of expenses. The Court relied on Hasmat Rai v. Raghunath Prasad and M/s Variety Emporium v. V.R.M. Mohd. Ibrahim Naina for the principle that subsequent events may be considered and relief moulded accordingly. It also held that repairs must be distinguished from structural alteration or reconstruction.

rule.if: unsafe_building_eviction_proceeding and subsequent_event_before_final_relief and tenant_completed_nonstructural_repairs and premises_safe_after_repairs

predicates.unsafe_building_eviction_proceeding: A landlord seeks eviction because a building is alleged to be unsafe or unfit for human habitation.
predicates.subsequent_event_before_final_relief: An event affecting the need for relief occurs before the court finally determines the relief.
predicates.tenant_completed_nonstructural_repairs: The tenant completed repairs that did not amount to structural alteration or reconstruction.
predicates.premises_safe_after_repairs: The repairs made the premises safe and fit for habitation.

issues.definition: In an unsafe-building eviction proceeding, if the tenant completes nonstructural repairs that make the premises safe before final relief is determined, the need for eviction no longer subsists.
